raw:
Approach: the strongest interactions in NAS-Bench-201 are replacement effects (an edit gains most when it replaces `none`, and loses most when it removes a strong conv), connectivity effects (an edit on a path matters less when that path is cut elsewhere), and diminishing returns when parallel edges into node 3 are already strong conv layers. I have not run any benchmark data, so the probabilities below are my own estimates and none of them is verified. I put the replacement hypotheses at about 0.8–0.9, the connectivity ones at about 0.6–0.7, and the diminishing-returns ones at about 0.5–0.6. An intuitive reader would likely accept the replacement and connectivity ones and doubt the diminishing-returns ones.
